name: Defend the Rider

modes.text: This token saddles Mounts and crews Vehicles as though its power were 2 greater.

notes: The two "• …" bullets belong to the "Choose one —" line the spell ability claims (faceLines drops bullets). The Pilot token's own ability is carried as the token's `text` only.

issues: • Create a 1/1 colorless Pilot creature token with "This token saddles Mounts and crews Vehicles as though its power were 2 greater." — expected The created token carries a functional static ability: when tapped to pay a crew cost (or to saddle a Mount) its power counts as 2 greater, so a lone 1/1 Pilot can pay crew 3 / saddle 3. — scripted The quoted ability is carried only as the token op's decorative `text` field. schema-core.ts:639-641 lets `text` through, but TokenSpec (state.ts:10) has no text/abilities member and game.ts:1373-1382 builds tok.token from name/power/toughness/colors/types/subtypes/keywords only — the string is dropped at runtime. Nothing in the engine implements an 'as though its power were N greater' adjustment either: cost.ts:103-104 and game.ts:695 (pickCrew) sum raw power(s,o). The clause is therefore 100% non-functional; the renderer scores this bullet LOW 0.00 ('the rendering does not print 2') yet the card still scores 1.00 through the gate. Blind scenario 4 ('The Pilot token crews a Vehicle with crew 3 on its own') fails at the crew activation with 'no legal action matched for P0 (have: pass)', which is exactly this gap. — CR CR 702.122b (crew), 702.190b (saddle), 613.1 / 611 (as-though effects)

• Create a 1/1 colorless Pilot creature token … — expected A token with no name in its text is named for its subtypes — this token's name is 'Pilot' (CR 111.4). — scripted `name` is omitted, so game.ts:1377 falls back to `${e.subtypes.join(' ')} token` = 'Pilot token'. Blind scenario 3 fails both the pt and control expectations with 'no object named Pilot'. Arguably an engine naming convention rather than a rules error (the emit at game.ts:1383 does use the bare 'Pilot'), but the script could have pinned name:'Pilot' and did not, and it is the proximate cause of a second blind-scenario failure. — CR CR 111.4

covers / notes — expected A script that cannot express a clause should surface it as an open need, not pass verification as 'verified' with an empty `covers`. — scripted covers: [] and the note only says the ability is 'carried as the token's `text` only'. Honest, but the script is marked status 'verified' with problems: [] while a full printed ability does nothing; 2/4 blind scenarios fail. — CR n/a

Choose one — • Target permanent you control gains hexproof and indestructible until end of turn. — expected Exactly one mode chosen on cast; a single targeted permanent you control gains both keywords until end of turn. — scripted choose-mode count 1 with two mode arrays, and grant-keyword target {kind:'permanent',controller:'you'} keywords ['hexproof','indestructible'] duration 'eot' — correct, including that a noncreature permanent is a legal target. Both blind scenarios covering this mode pass. No defect here. — CR CR 700.2, 601.2c, 702.11b, 702.12b
